What We Do

Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure.

Role at a Glance

Gecko Robotics is seeking an Embedded Software Engineering Intern to join RoboSPLAT within Field Infra in Pittsburgh for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.

RoboSPLAT builds software and tools that help teams develop, deploy, debug, and operate Gecko’s robotic and ultrasonic testing (UT) collection systems. You will work primarily in C/C++ and Python on a defined project that improves system integration, diagnostics, testing, or development workflows.

What you will do

- Develop C/C++ and Python software for a defined embedded software project under the guidance of experienced engineers.

- Build or improve tooling, diagnostics, tests, or workflows that reduce friction in developing, debugging, and deploying software on robot hardware.

- Work across software and system boundaries by integrating services or hardware-facing interfaces, investigating system behavior, testing solutions, and documenting findings.

- Use version control, code review, and structured debugging practices to produce maintainable code.

- Collaborate with RoboSPLAT and partner teams, communicate status and tradeoffs clearly, and deliver a final demonstration and handoff.

Technologies We Use (If Applicable)

C/C++, Python, Git, Linux, networking, and ROS 2. Depending on the project, you may also work with the Yocto Project, NVIDIA Jetson Orin, cloud infrastructure, or Electron, React, and TypeScript.

About You

You are a hands-on engineering student who wants to understand how software behaves on real hardware. You work methodically, seek out missing knowledge, communicate clearly, and care about building tools and systems that others can use.

Required Skills

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related engineering discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.

- Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.

- Foundational programming experience in C/C++ and Python, including object-oriented programming.

- Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.

- Understanding of basic computer networking.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain findings and tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.

- Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback.

Preferred Skills

- Experience with ROS 2.

- Familiarity with embedded Linux systems or platforms such as the Yocto Project or NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

- Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP.

- Experience building applications with Electron, React, or TypeScript.

- Exposure to embedded communication protocols, microcontrollers, or real-time operating systems is a plus.

- Ability to work with basic electronic systems, read simple schematics, and use common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, and programmable power supplies.

Who We Are

At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off.

Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact.

Who We Are

HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab. Combining startup agility with HP’s global scale, we’re building intelligent technologies that redefine how the world works, creates, and collaborates.

We’re assembling a diverse, world-class team—engineers, designers, researchers, and product minds—focused on creating an intelligent ecosystem across HP’s portfolio. Together, we’re developing intuitive, adaptive solutions that spark creativity, boost productivity, and make collaboration seamless.

We create breakthrough solutions that make complex tasks feel effortless, teamwork more natural, and ideas more impactful—always with a human-centric mindset.

By embedding AI advancements into every HP product and service, we’re expanding what’s possible for individuals, organisations, and the future of work.

Join us as we reinvent work, so people everywhere can do their best work.

About the Role

HP IQ's Product Integrity & Developer Productivity team is responsible for building next-generation tools and systems that improve developer productivity and product quality at scale. We are specifically investing in agentic systems that automate complex workflows, from intelligent JIRA triage and root-cause analysis to test planning and quality automation. In this internship role, you will work directly with our hiring manager and team to design, build, and deploy agents that utilize pre-trained machine learning models to solve real problems for developers and quality engineers. This is an exceptional opportunity to be part of a team navigating the fundamental shift toward agentic development and to contribute meaningfully to tools that thousands of developers will rely on.

What You Might Do

As an intern on our team, you'll contribute to real-world engineering projects that explore how AI can improve the way software is built, tested, and maintained. Depending on business priorities and your team's needs, you may have the opportunity to:

- Design, build, and iterate on AI-powered tools and workflows that improve engineering productivity.

- Develop intelligent systems that help automate software development, testing, debugging, or quality assurance processes.

- Prototype and evaluate new approaches for applying large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI to solve complex engineering challenges.

- Collaborate with software engineers, machine learning engineers, product managers, designers, and other cross-functional partners to deliver impactful solutions.

- Participate in technical design discussions, code reviews, and collaborative problem-solving sessions.

- Analyze technical challenges, propose innovative solutions, and contribute fresh ideas that improve products, tools, and engineering workflows.

- Build, test, and iterate on production-quality software while learning modern engineering best practices.

- Present your work, share technical learnings, and contribute to a collaborative engineering culture.

Essential Qualifications

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor's or graduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

- Solid understanding of coding fundamentals and comfort with at least one programming language; you should be able to learn new languages and frameworks as needed.

- Familiarity with agentic systems, AI tools (such as Claude Code or OpenAI), or model utilization in applications; deep machine learning expertise is not required as we focus on using pre-trained models, not building them.

- Ability to break down complex problems into manageable steps and solve them independently while knowing when to ask for help.

- Willingness to question established processes and propose alternative approaches; comfort in an environment that values fresh thinking and continuous improvement.

- Strong communication skills; ability to explain your reasoning clearly and articulate the logic behind your technical choices.

- Familiarity with software development workflows, quality assurance, testing practices, or developer tooling (helpful but not required).

Preferred Skills

- Experience building or working with automation tools or systems that improve workflow efficiency.

- Exposure to or familiarity with JIRA, continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) systems, or testing frameworks.

- Experience working in cross-functional teams or in environments where you collaborated with people from different technical backgrounds.

- Understanding or coursework in machine learning, AI, or agent systems.

- Example projects demonstrating agentic thinking, such as personal projects using AI tools to automate tasks.

Hourly Pay Range: $45.00–$51.00 per hour. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as skills, qualifications, and experience.

2027 Internship Program Dates: May/June–August/September 2027. Final dates will be based on student schedules.

Compensation & Benefits (Full-Time Employees)

The salary range for this role is listed above. Final salary offered is based upon multiple factors including individual job-related qualifications, education, experience, knowledge and skills.

- Health insurance

- Dental insurance

- Vision insurance

- Long term/short term disability insurance

- Employee assistance program

- Flexible spending account

- Life insurance

- Generous time off policies, including;

- 4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure

- 11 paid holidays

- Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave (US benefits overview)

HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab, building the intelligence to empower humanity—reimagining how we work, create, and connect to shape the future of work.

Work with the speed and focus of a startup, backed by HP’s scale.

We learn fast, stay future-focused, and imagine what comes next—together.

Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

ENGINEERING - EPIC GAMES SERVICES

What We Do

Driving the plug-in power behind Unreal Engine 5. We bridge connections for licensees and our own internal game teams to online services. This allows games like Fortnite to utilize a combination of platform online services as well as Epic’s own online services to build cross-platform online features. Login, parties, voice chat, matchmaking, purchasing, cloud storage, and analytics are just a few examples of online features that our Online Game Services team helps games utilize.

FRONTEND PROGRAMMER INTERN

What You'll Do

The Social Web team builds the interfaces players use to connect with other players across Epic's ecosystem, including Fortnite, Rocket League, and Fall Guys. As an intern on the team, you'll ship real features that touch millions of players, gaining hands-on experience with production web development while being mentored through the full lifecycle of a feature, from design to deployment.

In this role, you will

- Build and ship features using React, JavaScript, and TypeScript, working directly in our production codebase

- Partner with senior engineers to design and implement UI components and user flows for the social overlay experience

- Debug issues and contribute fixes across the front end, with guidance from your team

- Participate in code reviews, both giving and receiving feedback, to build strong engineering habits

- Take ownership of a well-scoped project or feature over the course of your internship, from planning through to shipping

What we're looking for

- Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science or a related field

- Coursework or project experience with JavaScript and/or TypeScript

- Familiarity with React or another modern front-end framework

- A strong interest in distributed systems

Internship positions are located at PIMCO’s Newport Beach, CA Headquarters

You're eligible to apply if you:

- Pursuing an undergraduate degree

- Must be able to begin full time employment at a PIMCO office between January 2028 – August 2028

- Are business proficient in English

- Show a strong interest in the financial markets, macroeconomics, investments, finance

- Have strong work ethic and integrity; you should be a team player that is proactive and self-motivated

- Have the ability to work effectively on multiple projects simultaneously

- Are comfortable with handling ambiguity

- Possess outstanding analytical and mathematical skills

- Demonstrate curiosity and experience in using new emerging technologies and AI tools in your work or school projects to solve problems and drive better outcomes

- Analyzing and developing trade ideas in fixed income products

- Support Senior Portfolio Managers in terms of managing client accounts

PIMCO’s Portfolio Management team creates and supports investment solutions designed to help clients meet their financial goals while navigating decades of market change. You will work alongside Portfolio Managers on the desk, focusing on supporting the execution and optimization of trades and required research. Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to work with the design, production and quality teams to develop and qualify process to make rocket engines. Rocket Lab’s Manufacturing team are the builders and the doers who work with our advanced machinery across our global manufacturing sites to get our satellites, satellite components, and rockets out the door.

- Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges

- Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates

- Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

- GPA of 3.5 or above

- Solid Modelling experience

- Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) experience

- Finite Elements Analysis (FEA) experience

- CNC, mills, lathes, and powered equipment experience

- Geometric Dimension & Tolerancing (GD&T) experience

- Siemens NX, Jira, Solidworks, ANSYS experience

- 3D Printing experience

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

- Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning January, February, or March 2027

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

$28—$28 USD

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. What You Get Out of the Internship​​

At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​

- Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​

- Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​

- Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​

- Be a part of an innovative team and culture​

Who we want​​

Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​

Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​

Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​

Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​

Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​

Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better.

Opportunities Available​

​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams:

Research & Development

New Product Development

R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production.

Product Engineering

R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products.

Test Lab

Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you!

Majors Targeted: Mechanical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Material Science Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Automation/Mechatronics Engineering

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships

- Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities

Your Role:

- Job Description: Robotics Data Operator Intern

- Category: Robotics / AI Data Operator

- Location: LA, US

As the Intern of the Robotics Data Factory, you will be responsible for collecting high-fidelity human behavior and robot teleoperation data. This data is essential for training the next generation of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, helping robots learn to perceive and interact with the physical world by capturing real-world human interactions and precision robotic movements.

Key Responsibilities

- Egocentric Data Collection: Wear designated head-mounted recording devices (e.g., smartphone rigs, GoPro, or head-mounted VR kits) to capture daily or industrial tasks from a first-person perspective in diverse environments (home, retail, or manufacturing).

- VR Teleoperation: Operate robotic systems via VR interfaces to perform complex manipulation tasks. Ensure high-quality capture of multi-modal data, including joint states, torques, and gripper status, while maintaining low-latency execution.

- Technical Specification Compliance: Maintain strict recording standards (1080p, 30FPS, horizontal orientation, FOV >130°). Ensure accurate extraction of camera intrinsic parameters and time-synchronization across all sensors.

- Quality Assurance & Pre-processing: Conduct initial self-inspections to filter out clips with excessive shaking, occlusions, or focus failures. Ensure data is correctly formatted (e.g., MCAP, HDF5) and uploaded according to protocol.

Basic Qualifications:

- Experience: 0–1 years of experience. Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.

- Extreme Attention to Detail: Ability to strictly follow complex technical guidelines regarding framing, motion rhythm, and lighting environments.

- Technical Proficiency: Comfortable using smartphones, VR hardware (Meta Quest/HTC Vive), and various digital accessories. Basic understanding of video recording parameters and calibration.

- Action Consistency: Ability to perform tasks naturally while maintaining the specific "robotic-friendly" pacing required for imitation learning.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience in Python, Linux command line.

- Familiarity with ROS2, LeRobot, or AI data labeling workflows.

- Strong interest in Embodied AI and robotics.

Work Environment & Restrictions:

- Glove Policy: Preference for bare hands; if necessary, only approved thin/transparent medical gloves are allowed. No thick or dark-colored gloves that obscure finger articulation.

- Safety & Privacy: Must follow all site-specific safety protocols and strictly avoid capturing any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or sensitive/prohibited scenarios.

Perks + Benefits

- Casual dress code + relaxed work environment

- Culturally diverse, progressive atmosphere

Faraday Future is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Ground Systems Deployment Team

The Ground Systems Deployment and Construction team is responsible for turning bare ground into functional drone charging sites! We’re a broad, cross-functional team with skills across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, and construction engineering with a mandate to deliver world-class construction execution with zero issues in the first 30 days, on-time and on-budget, using scalable, cost-optimized, and serviceable designs.

The Role

The Ground System Deployment and Construction Engineering team is seeking a curious, collaborative Electrical Engineering Intern to support the design and deployment of Zipline’s Ground Systems across a variety of sites and applications.

In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience with commercial and light-industrial electrical distribution as applied to an autonomous drone delivery network. Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll help with utility coordination, site-level electrical design, structure-level wiring approaches, and technical documentation.

You’ll collaborate with mechanical, structural, electrical, and deployments teams to support real-world projects and contribute to problem-solving as new challenges arise. This internship also offers opportunities to explore new design ideas and assist with improvements to our engineering processes. You’ll work and become familiar with the National Electrical Code and apply the concepts to site and infrastructure designs.

The internship is based in South San Francisco, with occasional travel within California and the U.S. for site visits or field support.

What You'll Do

- Support engineers with research, drafting, and documentation for electrical distribution and structure-level wiring designs aligned with NEC and relevant standards.

- Assist with UL/TUV certification efforts by gathering documentation, preparing technical materials, and coordinating with engineering partners.

- Help prepare materials, track communication, and support interactions with deployment and construction teams

- Implement feedback from Deployment and Construction teams to continuously optimize designs for more efficient build and scale

- Design electrical distribution of commercial and light industrial ground system projects per NEC and relevant applicable codes and standards.

- Design next generation charging structure level electrical wiring and installation approaches.

- Evaluate all options and a lean budget, select best vendors to ensure reliable and quality services and products.

- Help document project risks, prepare materials for meetings, support communication across teams, and occasionally participate in site visits for field observations.

- Create documentation to ensure quality and process refinement between each build to help with consistent scale

- Collaborate with engineering and business teams to understand customer needs and contribute to improvements in Ground Systems infrastructure.

- Travel to commercial and flight test sites may be required on an ad hoc basis.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies, with relevant coursework (e.g., circuits, power systems, construction). Master's and PhD students are also eligible.

- Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a willingness to ask questions and learn.

- Familiarity with engineering tools or concepts such as CAD/ECAD, electrical modeling, or basic simulation software. (Revit, Bluebeam Revu, AutoCAD, NX)

- Clear written and verbal communication skills, especially when summarizing technical information.

- Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment and support a wide range of tasks.

- Curiosity, initiative, and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
Comfort with hands-on work and openness to occasional travel (if needed).

- An open mind to help us bring Zipline’s service to new and existing customers!

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September).

The hourly rate for this internship is $44 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

About the Institute of Foundation Models

The Institute of Foundation Models is dedicated to advancing the science and engineering of large-scale AI systems. Our researchers and engineers develop cutting-edge foundation models while pushing the limits of high-performance computing and efficient AI inference. By combining deep expertise in machine learning, systems engineering, and hardware optimization, we build scalable AI solutions that drive scientific discovery and real-world impact.

As part of the team, interns work alongside world-class researchers and performance engineers to optimize the execution of large-scale foundation models on next-generation NVIDIA GPU architectures. This internship provides hands-on experience in low-level GPU performance analysis, kernel optimization, and hardware-aware inference acceleration.

Key Responsibilities

This intensive internship offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the development of a simulator and profiling framework for foundation model inference on NVidia GPUs.

Responsibilities include:

- Develop analytical performance models for GPU kernels and inference workloads.

- Build and validate a simulator to estimate theoretical hardware performance limits.

- Compare measured kernel performance against architectural peak throughput.

- Identify performance bottlenecks in compute, memory, communication, and scheduling.

- Analyze GPU execution using NVIDIA Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute.

- Investigate PTX and SASS code generation to understand low-level execution behavior.

- Collaborate with researchers and engineers to optimize inference kernels for transformer-based models.

- Evaluate utilization of Tensor Cores, memory bandwidth, caches, and instruction pipelines.

- Design profiling methodologies for Hopper and Blackwell architectures.

- Document findings and provide actionable recommendations for performance improvements.

Academic Qualifications

Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing, or a related quantitative discipline.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with CUDA programming and GPU kernel development.

- Understanding of NVIDIA GPU architecture and memory hierarchy.

- Familiarity with performance profiling tools such as Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute.

- Knowledge of PTX, SASS, and low-level GPU execution.

- Experience optimizing CUDA kernels for throughput and latency.

- Understanding of roofline analysis, performance modeling, and hardware utilization metrics.

- Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

- Strong programming skills in C++, CUDA, and Python.

Desired Skills

- Performance engineering mindset.

- Strong analytical and debugging abilities.

- Interest in AI systems, inference optimization, and hardware-software co-design.

- Ability to work independently on research and engineering challenges.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
